Hickes, George
    D.D. 13.9.1677.
    ‘Coll. Lincoln. Oxon. Socius & chaplain to Duke of Lauderdale’.
    Born 21.6.1642 at Moorhouse, Newsham 2nd son of William Hickes and Elizabeth Kay/Key.
    Attended school at Northallerton.
     Apprenticed to a Plymouth merchant
     he entered Oxford, St John’s College April 1659,
     but migrated to Magdalen. M.A. 23.5.1664.
    Tutor Lincoln College. Travelled abroad.
     Chaplain to Duke of Lauderdale 1676 -.
     Vicar All Hallows, Barking 1680 – 86.
     Rector Alvechurch 1686 - .
     Was also Dean of Worcester. Deprived 1691.
     Non jurant Bishop.
     Published on ecclesiastical controversies and on patristic and philological scholarship.
     D.D. Oxford 1679.
     St Andrews D.D. was for Ravillac redivius (1678), an account of the trial of James Mitchell.
    Publications.
    Died 13.12.1715.

Sanders, William
    Received in album as professor of philosophy St Leonard’s College 12.2.1672.
    Born c. 1640 where and parentage unknown but was brother of the Glasgow printer Robert Sanders elder whose origin is likewise unknown.
    Educated at Marischal College Aberdeen M.A. 24.6.1659.
     Described as divinity student on 10 Aug 1659 when he was appointed under master of Aberdeen Grammar School.
     Presented by Archbishop Sharp as Regent St Leonard’s College 5.11.1671. Still regent 19.2.1675 but demitted office in this year on appointment to 
    Professorship of mathematics at St Andrews. Professor until at least 1.3.1688 but demitted by 5.11.1688 when his successor was presented.
     Described as schoolmaster in Dundee 17.3.1690,
     when he was elected Rector of Perth Grammar School. Demitted on pension 16.10.1704.
     Taught privately in Edinburgh until at least 20.12.1705.
    Publications.

    Received in album 2.4.1702 (? = honorary degree). ‘idque tam ob multiplices Minervae dotes qui ob singularia in academia in beneficia’,
    ‘Writer to the Signet’.
    Baptised 24.3.1667 4th son of Sir Robert Pringle of Stichell.
    Probably studied Edinburgh – M.A. 3.4.1684. 
    Admitted Writer to the Signet 10.5.1693.
    Treasurer of the Society of Writers to the Signet 1697 – 98.

     Deputy Keeper of the Signet 1716 – 25.
    Died December 1735.

Murdison, John
    M.A. 1587, minus potens.
    ? also M.A. Edinburgh August 1587.
    ?Born c. 1568 eldest son of Andrew Murdison, merchant, Edinburgh.
    Helmstadt University as a medical student 1588, 1589.
     Matriculated Jena c. 1589.

     Teaching at Middelburg 1592 – c. 1599,

Pitcairn, Archibald
    Received in album 2.8.1684. Probably tantamount to an honorary degree.
    Born 25.12.1652 son of Alexander Pitcairn, merchant, Edinburgh and Janet Sydserff.
    Studied at Edinburgh University – M.A. 20.3.1671.
     Also studied law at Paris
     and medicine at Rheims – M.D. 13.8.1680.
    Began to practise in Edinburgh c. 1681.
     Professor of physic at Leyden 1692.
     Resigned and returned to Edinburgh 1693.
    One of the promoters of the Royal College of Physicians in Edinburgh 1681.
    Publications. Hon. M.D. King’s College, Aberdeen 7.8.1699.
    Died 1713.
    
      Innes Smith

Philip, James (Philpe)
    Matriculated from St Salvator’s College 1671/72 (9.2.1672).
    M.A. 24.7.1675, potens.
    Born c. 1656 son of James Philip of Almerieclose.
    Attended Arbroath Grammar School.

    Succeeded father in Almerieclose inc. 1695/96.
    Wrote ‘Grameid’, said to be last attempt at a Latin epic in Britain, concerning the rising of 1689 in which he was involved with Viscount Dundee. It was not published until 1888.
